nodes.label: Consistent Error Envelope (code/message/details)
nodes.rationale: Raw driver errors and stack traces are never returned, so internals are not exposed to callers.

nodes.label: POST /v1/vault/folders
nodes.rationale: Folder name is unique per user because the mention token is derived from the name with spaces replaced by dashes; collisions return 409.

nodes.label: DELETE /v1/vault/files/{fileId}
nodes.rationale: Removes both the metadata row and the Supabase Storage object so the two tiers cannot drift.

nodes.label: DELETE /v1/vault/folders/{folderId}
nodes.rationale: Cascades to every contained file across storage and rows rather than orphaning them.

nodes.label: GET /v1/vault/folders
nodes.rationale: Returns folders with nested file metadata in one call so the library view and @ mention suggestions can be seeded together.

nodes.label: GET /v1/vault/mentions
nodes.rationale: Returns folders and files as a single token list capped at 8 (max 20) so @ autocomplete stays responsive.

nodes.label: Mention Token (@Folder/file)
nodes.rationale: A stable human-typable handle that lets Chat Agent and Spec Design Agent reference vault items; messages send mentions: string[] alongside message so the agent can hydrate file contents before LLM generation.

nodes.label: ok/data/error Response Envelope
nodes.rationale: Every response carries a boolean ok discriminant so clients branch on one field regardless of status code.

nodes.label: Spec Design Agent (Vault Consumer)
nodes.rationale: Uploads are temp-first conceptually, but for v1 the agent uploads directly into a folder after the user confirms persist.

nodes.label: POST /v1/vault/files
nodes.rationale: Multipart upload capped at 20MB (413 otherwise) with an allowlist of accepted MIME types; bytes go to {userId}/{folderId}/{fileId}-{filename}.

nodes.label: features/vault/service.ts Client
nodes.rationale: Frontend calls {AGENT_API}/v1/vault from a single service module configured by NEXT_PUBLIC_AGENT_API and NEXT_PUBLIC_VAULT_TOKEN.

nodes.label: Aster Design System Priority
nodes.rationale: Four-step component priority ending in a custom accessible component; Flowbite, MUI, and Emotion are legacy and migrated opportunistically rather than expanded.

nodes.label: JavaScript Bundle Optimization
nodes.rationale: A hidden component still executes hooks, fetches, and loads dependencies, so display:none / inactive tabs / closed modals must be split or conditionally mounted rather than assumed free.

nodes.label: CI Quality Gates
nodes.rationale: GitLab CI includes an externally maintained aster-web pipeline, so the full job list is invisible from this repo and required-check changes must be coordinated with that pipeline.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits Convention
nodes.rationale: Commitlint, Commitizen, and Husky are not configured, so Conventional Commits remain a team convention rather than an automatically enforced rule.

nodes.label: Feature-Based Folder Structure
nodes.rationale: Route files stay thin and compose feature modules; each feature owns its components, hooks, form.ts, service.ts, and types.ts so a capability has one clear domain owner.

nodes.label: Forms With React Hook Form and Zod
nodes.norm_label: forms with react hook form and zod
nodes.rationale: Schema, inferred type via z.infer, defaults, and the form hook live together in form.ts; an explicit toAPIData mapper converts form values to API input so validation stays UI-independent.

nodes.label: Python pre-commit Framework
nodes.rationale: Used instead of Husky for trailing whitespace, private-key detection, and ESLint; the configured pre-push script performs no checks so it must not be treated as a quality gate.

nodes.label: Current Project Stack
nodes.rationale: Next.js 15 App Router, React 18, strict TS, static export, Bun, Tailwind 3 + Aster/HeroUI, TanStack Query, RHF+Zod, Zustand, Sentry. Adding a second library for an existing stack responsibility requires an architecture discussion.

nodes.label: Frontend Service Layer
nodes.rationale: Endpoint functions own URL construction and transport but never render UI, toast, navigate, or set component state; backend errors are normalized at the service/query boundary and unstable responses validated with Zod.

nodes.label: Tailwind and Design Tokens
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary values are avoided when a token exists, and dynamic class fragments are banned because Tailwind cannot statically detect them.

nodes.label: TanStack Query Conventions
nodes.rationale: Stable array query keys that include every parameter, feature-level key factories, narrowest invalidation after a mutation, and no copying query data into local state - the cache stays the single owner of remote state.

nodes.label: POST /chat Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Stateful across turns via a returned threadId that the caller must echo back on later turns.

nodes.label: Chat GUI Runtime
nodes.rationale: Browser chat over HTTP that deliberately does not edit a product workspace - it emits JSON artifacts only.

nodes.label: frontend/CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md Pointer
nodes.rationale: A one-line @AGENTS.md include keeps a single source of agent rules shared across Claude Code and other runtimes.

nodes.label: Vault API
nodes.rationale: Knowledge library split by storage tier - file bytes in Supabase Storage, metadata in Postgres - so listings and mention autocomplete stay cheap relational queries.

nodes.label: Frontend Conventions
nodes.rationale: Uses must/should/may requirement levels and applies only to new or materially changed code, so existing code is not rewritten just to match the guide.

nodes.label: Next.js create-next-app Starter README
nodes.rationale: Unmodified create-next-app boilerplate; it offers npm/yarn/pnpm/bun interchangeably, which conflicts with the Bun-only rule in the conventions guide.

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes versus model training data, so the agent must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code rather than relying on memory.

nodes.label: Accessibility Requirements
nodes.rationale: Accessibility is a release requirement, not follow-up work; lint rules cannot prove it so the actual interaction must be reviewed and tested.

nodes.label: Server/Client Boundary Policy
nodes.rationale: 'use client' is added only when state, effects, handlers, browser APIs, or client providers are used, and boundaries stay as low as practical to reduce shipped JavaScript.

nodes.label: Effects Usage Policy
nodes.rationale: useEffect only synchronizes React with an external system - not for derived values, user actions, state resets, or fetching already handled by TanStack Query; effects must clean up and must not be async themselves.

nodes.label: Environment Variables and Security
nodes.rationale: Every NEXT_PUBLIC_ value is assumed visible to users, so no secret or privileged token may live in frontend env files; config is read through a typed src/config/env.ts helper and validated early.

nodes.label: Error Handling and Observability
nodes.rationale: Users get plain-language messages while the original error is preserved for Sentry; production console output is stripped so console logging is not an observability strategy.

nodes.label: Memoization Policy
nodes.rationale: Memoization has maintenance and runtime cost, so useCallback/useMemo/memo are applied only on profiling evidence or a genuine stable-reference requirement.

nodes.label: Bun vs Yarn packageManager Ambiguity
nodes.rationale: package.json declares Yarn in packageManager while README and active scripts use Bun; Bun is the team convention and the metadata should be aligned separately to avoid ambiguous tooling.

nodes.label: Performance Practices
nodes.rationale: Optimize only with measured evidence - React DevTools, browser tools, or ANALYZE=true bun run build:nonprd - never speculatively.

nodes.label: Prettier As Formatting Authority
nodes.rationale: Automated tools settle formatting so style is never debated in review; tabs, no semicolons, single quotes, 120 cols, sorted imports and sorted Tailwind classes including inside tv.

nodes.label: State Ownership Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Seven-step ladder from derived value up to a Zustand store - always pick the narrowest owner, and never park query responses or secrets in a store.

nodes.label: Static Export Constraint
nodes.rationale: Because output is "export", Route Handlers, Server Actions, server-only rendering assumptions, and Next image optimization are unavailable without changing the deployment architecture.

nodes.label: TypeScript Strict Conventions
nodes.rationale: No any, no @ts-ignore (only @ts-expect-error with a reason), no non-null assertions - the aim is to make invalid states difficult to represent.

nodes.label: Backend/Frontend Port and CORS Alignment
nodes.rationale: Next and Express both default near 3000, so PORT and CORS_ORIGIN must be set explicitly to avoid a collision.

nodes.label: Pagination Convention (limit/offset + deterministic ORDER BY)
nodes.rationale: Default limit 20, max 100, and an always-present deterministic ORDER BY so paged results are stable.

nodes.label: Architecture Design Areas
nodes.rationale: Five fixed lenses - architecture, integration, data ownership, scalability, security - so no dimension is silently skipped.

nodes.label: Mermaid erDiagram From FK Graph
nodes.rationale: Cardinality is taken from the FK direction and nullability reported by inspect_relationships, not from intuition.

nodes.label: Specification Contents
nodes.rationale: Fixed sections - scope, entities with grain, field mapping, rules, edge cases - so ambiguity has nowhere to hide.

nodes.label: Test Coverage Matrix
nodes.rationale: Covers happy path per advertised status plus 400/401/403/404/409, nullability that describe_tables actually permits, pagination with deterministic ORDER BY and empty page, and timestamptz stored UTC converted at the boundary.

nodes.label: Naming and File Conventions
nodes.rationale: handle... for local handlers vs on... for callback props, boolean names that read as a question, and one domain term reused across routes, UI, types, API functions, and tests.

nodes.label: Bifrost LLM Gateway
nodes.rationale: Routes every phase through the company gateway; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is only needed when a model id is anthropic:… and is unused with the gateway.

nodes.label: Claude Code Runtime
nodes.rationale: Chosen when the analyst/architect must write specs and SQL directly into the product repo tree; gets skills, subagents and MCP tools.

nodes.label: Codex Runtime
nodes.rationale: Has no plugin equivalent of Claude Code subagents, so agents/*.md is not loaded; phase discipline must come from skills and memory/AGENTS.md instead.

nodes.label: Knowledge Ingestion Pipeline
nodes.rationale: search_api_specs and search_schema_docs are useless until Confluence pages and DDL are indexed, so ingestion is a documented prerequisite.

nodes.label: sa-agent Plugin Marketplace
nodes.rationale: Two manifests (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json and .agents/plugins/marketplace.json) point at one plugin so both runtimes load identical skills, MCP servers, and memory.

nodes.label: sa-knowledge MCP Server
nodes.rationale: Spawned MCP processes always load backend/.env by absolute path so tools keep working when cwd is a foreign product repo.

nodes.label: Backend Skill
nodes.rationale: Endpoints must be directly implementable against the real schema, so every response field is traced to a column before the contract is written.

nodes.label: Jira Skill (Discuss Only)
nodes.rationale: Jira is explicitly not a default source of truth; it is loaded only when the user names a ticket, and never for schema, API, SQL, plan, or execute work.

nodes.label: Solution Architect Skill
nodes.rationale: Design is grounded in the live FK graph first because entity coupling constrains where service boundaries can legally be drawn.

nodes.label: System Analyst Skill
nodes.rationale: Goal is a spec a backend engineer can build without follow-up questions, so every field is traced to a real column or an explicit derivation rule.

nodes.label: Test Engineer Skill
nodes.rationale: Tests assert the published contract recovered from search_api_specs rather than an imagined one; the skill is read-only and never inserts rows.

nodes.label: SKILL.template.md Skill Template
nodes.rationale: Canonical four-section shape - Procedure, Rules, Examples - so every skill grounds work in live data before producing output.

nodes.label: sa-agent Capability Provider
nodes.rationale: Packaged as a provider checkout kept at a stable path so multiple product repos can point at one installation instead of vendoring the tooling per repo.

nodes.label: API Contract Requirements
nodes.rationale: Only failures the handler can actually produce are documented, and nullability is taken from describe_tables rather than guessed.

nodes.label: Backend Data Access Rules
nodes.rationale: Parameterized queries only ($1, no interpolation), validation at the edge, transactions with a stated isolation level, and an explicit flag when a WHERE/join column lacks an index.

nodes.label: Endpoint Conventions
nodes.rationale: Payload identifiers stay camelCase while DB columns stay snake_case and are mapped at the boundary, so column names the caller has no contract for never leak.

nodes.label: One Issue Key Per Call Rule
nodes.norm_label: one issue key per call rule
nodes.rationale: No unprompted searching or board-wide fan-out; quote only what Jira returned and never invent ticket fields.

nodes.label: Decision Records
nodes.rationale: Every significant choice records the decision, the alternatives, the deciding trade-off, and the consequence being accepted, so later readers can re-evaluate the call.

nodes.label: Markdown List Formatting Rule
nodes.rationale: Lists must be real lists with a blank line before them, one item per line - numbered items collapsed into a paragraph do not render.

nodes.label: Mermaid Diagram Policy
nodes.rationale: Always Mermaid never ASCII so output is renderable; every node and edge label is quoted because unquoted labels break on spaces, punctuation, and reserved words. Prose alone is not an architecture.

nodes.label: Gap List (Questions Not Inventions)
nodes.rationale: What the story asks for that the schema, index, or prior code does not support is listed as questions rather than invented, keeping the spec honest.

nodes.label: System Analyst SQL Rules
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL dialect, $1 parameters never interpolation, joins only along real foreign keys with stated cardinality, deterministic ORDER BY when paginating, and aggregations declaring their grain in a comment.

nodes.label: Minimal Grounded Fixtures
nodes.rationale: Fixture fields map to real columns and setup joins follow the live FK graph; keep only the columns the assertion needs and prefer the product repo's existing test runner and layout.

nodes.label: Frontmatter Trigger Convention
nodes.rationale: The agent reads only the frontmatter at startup, so the description's triggers decide whether the rest of the file is ever loaded - making trigger wording the highest-leverage part of a skill.

nodes.label: Specific and Testable Rules Convention
nodes.rationale: Rules must be checkable - 'parameters as $1, never interpolation' rather than the unverifiable 'write safe SQL'.

nodes.label: Grounding Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Ordered live DB first, indexed knowledge second, Jira only on explicit request - so answers are grounded in the schema that actually ships rather than in ticket prose.

nodes.label: One Phase At A Time Discipline
nodes.norm_label: one phase at a time discipline
nodes.rationale: Each artifact must be approved before the next phase runs, preventing the agent from coding against an unvalidated spec.

nodes.label: SA_AGENT_HOME Resolution
nodes.rationale: Codex spawns plugin MCP servers with a stripped environment and passes arguments verbatim, so the env var alone cannot locate the checkout; ~/.sa-agent/home is the fallback file the launcher reads.

nodes.label: Spec quiz (every rule has a test or is a gap)
